lead: A data bus is a set of wires plus rules (word format, timing, addressing and error check) that lets avionics boxes exchange digital data. ARINC 429 is the civil bus: one transmitter sends 32-bit labelled words to up to 20 receivers, in one direction only. MIL-STD-1553B is the military bus: one bus controller commands up to 31 remote terminals on a shared, dual-redundant cable at 1 Mbit/s. Both are decades old and still fitted, because they are simple, predictable and easy to certify.
prereq: You need: Avionics system architecture, IMA and LRUs.

blocks.text: ARINC 429 runs on a shielded twisted pair. The signal is bipolar return-to-zero: for a 1 the line goes to HI (+10 V between the wires) for the first half of the bit and returns to NULL (0 V); for a 0 it goes to LO (−10 V) and returns to NULL. Every bit returns to zero, so the receiver finds the clock from the data itself.

Only one transmitter may drive a pair, and up to 20 receivers listen. A box that must reply needs its own transmitter and its own pair, so a two-way link needs two pairs. One pair still carries many parameters: the transmitter sends a stream of words, each tagged with a label, and each receiver keeps the labels it needs. Two speeds are used: high speed at 100 kbit/s and low speed at 12 to 14.5 kbit/s (12.5 kbit/s is common). Words are separated by a gap of at least 4 bit times.

head: Bits
Field
Meaning
rows: which parameter this is, written in octal (for example 203); sent first
source/destination identifier: which of two similar units sent it, or who should use it
19 bits: binary (BNR, bit 29 is the sign), BCD digits or discrete bits
sign/status matrix; for BNR data: 11 normal, 01 no computed data, 10 functional test, 00 failure warning
set so the whole word has an odd number of 1s

blocks.where: T<sub>w</sub> is the time per word including the minimum 4-bit gap, in seconds; R is the bit rate in bit/s. The maximum word rate is 1 ÷ T<sub>w</sub>.

blocks.text: MIL-STD-1553B runs at 1 Mbit/s on a shielded twisted pair, with each box joined to the main cable by a transformer-coupled stub. Bits are Manchester II coded: a 1 is a high-to-low change in the middle of the bit and a 0 is low-to-high, so the clock travels with the data. The bus is normally dual redundant: cables A and B, and the controller retries on the other if a message fails.

One bus controller (BC) starts every transfer. Up to 31 remote terminals (RTs) speak only when commanded. A bus monitor listens and records traffic but never replies. Every word is 20 bit times: a 3-bit sync, 16 bits and an odd parity bit.

items: Command word (from the BC): RT address (5 bits), transmit/receive bit, subaddress (5 bits) and word count (5 bits, 1 to 32 data words).
Status word (from the RT): its own address plus flags such as message error, busy, subsystem flag and terminal flag.

blocks.text: In a receive transfer (BC to RT) the BC sends the command and the data words, and the RT answers with its status word. In a transmit transfer (RT to BC) the BC sends the command, and the RT answers with its status word followed by the data. Both carry one command, one status and n data words. The RT must reply within 4 to 12 µs. An RT-to-RT transfer uses two commands and two status words.

head: Feature
ARINC 429
MIL-STD-1553B
rows: one bus controller, up to 31 remote terminals

blocks.text: ARINC 429 suits one box broadcasting many values to many users, such as an air data computer feeding displays. 1553B suits many boxes that must talk both ways with confirmation, such as the mission computer, radar and stores management of a fighter. Newer airliners add switched Ethernet for higher rates (see AFDX and fibre-optic communication).

examples.question: An air data computer sends on one ARINC 429 bus: 12 labels at 50 times a second and 20 labels at 10 times a second. Each word is followed by the minimum 4-bit gap. (a) Find the word time and the maximum word rate at high speed (100 kbit/s). (b) Find the bus load. (c) Would the same traffic fit at low speed (12.5 kbit/s)? (d) The first 31 bits of one word contain fourteen 1s. What is bit 32?
steps: High speed: T<sub>w</sub> = 36 ÷ 100 000 = 0.36 ms. Maximum rate = 1 ÷ 0.00036 = 2778 words/s.
Load at high speed: 800 ÷ 2778 = 0.288, that is 28.8 % (check: 800 × 0.36 ms = 288 ms in each second).
Low speed: T<sub>w</sub> = 36 ÷ 12 500 = 2.88 ms; maximum rate = 347 words/s. 800 words/s is 800 ÷ 347 = 2.3 times the capacity, so it does not fit.
Parity: fourteen 1s is even, so bit 32 must be 1 to make fifteen, an odd number.
examples.answer: 0.36 ms per word and 2778 words/s maximum; the load is 28.8 % at high speed; at low speed it would need 230 % of the bus, so it does not fit; the parity bit is 1.

examples.question: On a 1553B bus the BC asks an RT to transmit 4 data words (RT to BC). The RT replies after 8 µs, and the BC leaves 4 µs before the next message. (a) Find the message time. (b) Show that a receive message with 4 data words takes the same time. (c) The BC polls 8 such RTs every 10 ms. Find the bus load.
steps: Transmit message: command 20 µs, response gap 8 µs, status 20 µs, 4 data words 80 µs, then 4 µs to the next message: 20 + 8 + 20 + 80 + 4 = 132 µs.
Receive message: command 20 µs, 4 data words 80 µs, response gap 8 µs, status 20 µs, gap 4 µs: also 132 µs. Both have one command, n data and one status word.
Load: 8 × 132 µs = 1056 µs in each 10 000 µs, that is 10.6 %.
examples.answer: Each message takes 132 µs either way; eight of them every 10 ms load the bus to about 10.6 %.

traps: Saying ARINC 429 needs one pair per parameter. It needs one pair per transmitter; one pair carries many labels.
Turning an ARINC 429 pair round for a reply. Only one transmitter may drive a pair.
Using 16 bits for the 1553B word time. The word on the wire is 20 bit times.
Giving a 1553B receive message an extra status word. Transmit and receive messages each have one status word.
Forgetting the 4-bit gap in ARINC 429 loading. A word occupies 36 bit times, not 32.

quiz.q: Give the bit fields of an ARINC 429 word.
Name the three 1553B word types and the three kinds of terminal.
quiz.a: Command, data and status words; bus controller, remote terminal and bus monitor.

quiz.q: How does an ARINC 429 receiver find its clock?
quiz.a: Every bit returns to NULL in its second half, so each bit gives a timing edge (bipolar return-to-zero).

quiz.q: Why is 1553B called a command/response bus?
quiz.a: Remote terminals never speak on their own; every transfer starts with a command from the bus controller, and the addressed terminal replies with a status word.

quiz.q: A 1553B transmit message carries 10 data words; the RT responds in 6 µs and the next message follows 4 µs later. Find the message time.
Units A and B must exchange 20 parameters each way. Compare the wiring with ARINC 429 and with 1553B.
quiz.a: ARINC 429: one pair from A to B and one pair from B to A, each carrying 20 labels: two pairs. 1553B: both units become terminals on the existing dual bus, and the BC schedules both directions; no new point-to-point pairs, but each transfer costs a command and a status word.

beyond: Not for the exam. On military aircraft, faster buses and Fibre Channel are added beside 1553B, which stays for control traffic. Search for 'ARINC 429 label list', 'MIL-STD-1553B mode codes' and 'ARINC 629'.
